slides.1.title: Hungarian White Wine Tasting Guide
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Ideal Serving Temperature
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Dry whites: 8–12°C; Aszú sweet wines: 12–14°C (slightly warmer allows the aromas to open); Eszencia: up to 16–18°C
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Glass Selection
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Dry Furmint: use a white Burgundy glass (tall and gently flared); Aszú: use a sweet wine glass (narrow mouth to concentrate the aromas)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Decoding Aroma Layers
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Primary (varietal): apricot, apple, lime; Secondary (yeast): bread, butter; Tertiary (aged): honey, smoke, mineral
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Decanting Advice
slides.1.highlights.3.content: Older vintages of dry Furmint may benefit from 30–60 minutes decanting; older vintage Aszú can be decanted 1–2 hours to let the complex aromas unfold
slides.1.content:
Tasting Hungarian white wines rewards careful attention — from the colour in the glass to the lingering acidity on the finish.

👁️ Visual Analysis

  • Dry Furmint: Pale gold to golden yellow, often with green tints
  • Tokaji Aszú: Deep gold to amber; old vintages show brownish-gold hues

👃 Aroma Categories

Fruit

Dry Furmint: apricot, yellow peach, apple
Aszú: apricot jam, candied orange peel

Floral

Furmint: white blossom, acacia
Hárslevelű: linden flower

Mineral

Flint, limestone, wet stone — the hallmark of volcanic terroir

Aged

Honey, beeswax, toasted hazelnut, cream — in mature Furmint

👄 Palate Analysis — The Key to Quality

Hungary's greatest hallmark is naturally high acidity. Even Aszú should display a clear acid backbone that balances the sweetness. If a sweet wine tastes "fat and cloying" with no acid support, it is usually poor quality. A good Aszú is crisp-sweet with layered complexity.
slides.2.title: Hungarian Red Wine Tasting Guide
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Serving Temperature
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Bikavér and medium-bodied reds: 16–18°C; top Villányi Franc: 17–19°C; lighter Kékfrankos: 14–16°C
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Decanting Advice
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Young Villányi Franc (3–8 years): decant 1–2 hours in advance or use a decanter; older vintages (10+ years): gentle pouring into a carafe is sufficient
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Red Wine Aroma Profiles
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Kékfrankos: dark cherry, blueberry, spice; Kadarka: rose, dried strawberry; Cabernet Franc (Villány): blackcurrant, violet, pencil shavings
slides.2.highlights.3.title: Ageing Potential
slides.2.highlights.3.content: Top Villányi Franc: 15–25 years; Egri Bikavér Superior: 8–15 years; everyday Kékfrankos: 3–8 years
slides.2.content:
Hungary's principal red varieties each have a distinct aroma and structural profile — understanding these distinctions is the foundation of serious tasting.

🍇 Three Variety Aroma Profiles

Kékfrankos
  • Dark cherry, blackcurrant, blueberry, violet
  • White pepper, spice
  • Mid-to-high acidity · medium tannin · fresh finish
Kadarka
  • Rose water, dried strawberry, wild red fruit
  • Spices — ginger, clove
  • Low tannin · medium acidity · fragrant and lingering
Cabernet Franc (Villány)
  • Blackcurrant, black plum, violet
  • Pencil shavings, cigar box
  • High ripe tannin · high acidity · long finish

⚡ Acidity Is Key

Compared to Bordeaux or Burgundy, Hungarian reds — especially Kékfrankos — tend to have more vibrant acidity, making them outstanding food wines. This character is particularly pronounced in cooler vintages from Sopron and Eger.
slides.3.title: Hungarian Wine and Traditional Cuisine Pairings
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Goulash (Gulyás)
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Kékfrankos or Egri Bikavér are the perfect partners — the spice notes mirror the paprika-rich flavours of the beef stew
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Danube Fish Soup (Halászlé)
slides.3.highlights.1.content: This bold, spicy fish soup is best cut through by an ice-cold dry Furmint or an Olaszrizling with good acidity
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Foie Gras
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Tokaji Aszú (3–4 Puttonyos) or dry Furmint makes a classic pairing with foie gras — especially in the Strasbourg tradition
slides.3.highlights.3.title: Dessert Pairings
slides.3.highlights.3.content: 6 Puttonyos Aszú with blue cheese or walnut cake; Eszencia is best enjoyed on its own — to savour the pure botrytis experience
slides.3.content:
Hungarian cuisine's bold paprika flavours and rich braised traditions make a natural foil for the country's wines, with their characteristic acidity and spice.

DishWineWhy It Works
Gulyás (beef stew) Egri Bikavér · Kékfrankos Acidity cuts the fat; spice complements the paprika
Halászlé (spicy fish soup) Dry Furmint · Olaszrizling High acidity cuts through the spice; minerality pairs with fresh fish
Foie Gras Tokaji Aszú 3–5 Puttonyos Sweet-acid balance cuts the rich fat
Rántott csirke (fried chicken) Szürkebarát · Furmint Acidity pairs with fried food; minerality enhances umami
Blue cheese (Gorgonzola) Tokaji Aszú 5–6 Puttonyos Honeyed sweetness balances the salty, pungent cheese
Chocolate dessert Villányi Franc · Szekszárdi Bikavér Red-fruit acidity creates complexity against cocoa bitterness

slides.4.content:
Congratulations on completing Level 1! You have covered a remarkable amount of ground — here is a summary of the core knowledge you have gained.

📜 Historical Status

  • 1737: world's first official classification (118 years before Bordeaux)
  • 22 PDOs covering 93,000 hectares
  • UNESCO World Heritage Site: Tokaj (2002)

🗺️ Geography and Climate

  • Carpathian Basin continental climate
  • Five major region groups: Tokaj · Upper Hungary · Pannon · Balaton · Duna

🍇 Key Varieties

  • White: Furmint (soul of Tokaj); Olaszrizling (most planted)
  • Red: Kékfrankos (most planted); Kadarka (traditional); Cabernet Franc (Villány)

🍷 Signature Wines

  • Sweet: Tokaji Aszú (botrytis · Furmint + Hárslevelű)
  • Red: Egri Bikavér (Bull's Blood · Kékfrankos dominant)

slides.5.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
When tasting a high-quality Tokaji Aszú, what is the most important sensation to look for?
A. Pure sweetness — the sweeter, the better
B. Sweet-acid balance: high residual sugar brings sweetness, but clear natural acidity keeps the palate fresh and prevents cloying
C. A very full body — the richer the texture, the higher the quality
D. Strong oak flavours indicating long barrel ageing

The defining quality marker of great Tokaji Aszú is the balance between its high residual sugar and its equally high natural acidity. An Aszú that is merely sweet — without the vibrant acid backbone — will feel heavy and cloying. Great Aszú should feel crisp and lively even at 6 Puttonyos level, with layers of honey, apricot and spice that continue to evolve long after swallowing.
What is the characteristic aroma profile of Kadarka?
A. Dark cherry, violet, graphite — very similar to Cabernet Franc
B. Rose water, dried strawberry, spices (ginger and clove), low tannin, lingering fragrance
C. Blackberry, cassis, licorice — rich and heavy
D. Green pepper, herbaceous notes, very high tannin

Kadarka is Hungary's most aromatic red variety. Its hallmark is an ethereal fragrance of rose water, dried strawberry and exotic spices (ginger, clove) combined with low tannin and medium acidity that gives it a delicate, lingering quality. In Egri Bikavér and Szekszárdi Bikavér blends, Kadarka plays the role of "aromatic contributor," complementing the structural backbone provided by Kékfrankos.
What is the traditional pairing for Hungarian Foie Gras?
A. Dry Furmint — high acidity cuts through the richness
B. Egri Bikavér — the red wine's tannins balance the fat
C. Tokaji Aszú sweet white wine — sweet-acid balance cuts through the rich fat
D. Szamorodni Száraz — oxidative style matches the intensity

Tokaji Aszú, particularly at 3–5 Puttonyos, is the classic partner for foie gras — both in the Hungarian culinary tradition and internationally. The wine's sweetness mirrors the richness of the liver, while its natural acidity (which remains high even in sweet styles) cuts through the fat and refreshes the palate, creating a harmonious balance.
Which of the following statements about Tokaj is correct?
A. Tokaj has approximately 93,000 hectares and is Hungary's largest wine region
B. Tokaj's classification was established in 1737 — 118 years before Bordeaux's 1855 classification
C. The main grape variety in Tokaji Aszú is Hárslevelű
D. The botrytis process destroys most of the natural acidity in the grapes

The correct answer is B. Tokaj's official vineyard classification was established in 1737 by Habsburg Emperor Charles VI — exactly 118 years before Bordeaux's 1855 Médoc classification (1855 − 1737 = 118). The other statements are incorrect: Tokaj has approximately 5,723 hectares (not 93,000 — that is Hungary's total vineyard area); the dominant variety in Tokaji Aszú is Furmint (not Hárslevelű); and botrytis actually concentrates and intensifies the acidity rather than destroying it — high natural acidity is one of Aszú's most important quality hallmarks.
slides.6.componentProps.slide.title: 📋 Level 1 Final Exam
In which year was the Tokaj wine region inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List?

The Tokaj Wine Region Historic Cultural Landscape was inscribed on the UNESCO World Cultural Heritage List in 2002. It is the only wine-cultural World Heritage Site in Hungary and one of the world's oldest legally defined wine regions.
Hungary's first official vineyard classification was established in 1737 — how many years before Bordeaux's 1855 Médoc classification?
A. 100 years
B. 155 years
C. 118 years
D. 200 years

1855 − 1737 = 118 years. In 1737, Habsburg Emperor Charles VI issued a decree formally classifying Tokaj's vineyards into First, Second and Third Class — the world's earliest known official vineyard classification system, predating Bordeaux's famous 1855 Médoc classification by 118 years.
Why is Furmint the ideal grape variety for producing Tokaji Aszú?
A. Furmint has very thick skin that makes it resistant to disease
B. Furmint has thin skin (allowing Botrytis to penetrate) and very high natural acidity (which balances the extreme sugar concentration in Aszú)
C. Furmint ripens very early, before autumn fog arrives
D. Furmint has the highest natural sugar content of any Hungarian variety

Furmint's thin skin allows Botrytis Cinerea hyphae to penetrate easily and initiate the noble rot process. Equally important is its very high natural acidity: even after the extreme sugar concentration of botrytis, Furmint retains enough acid to balance the sweetness, producing an Aszú that feels vibrant and lively rather than cloying.
Which is Hungary's most widely planted red grape variety?
A. Kadarka
B. Cabernet Franc
C. Kékfrankos
D. Merlot

Kékfrankos is Hungary's most widely planted red grape variety, with over 8,000 hectares under vine across virtually all 22 of Hungary's PDOs. It is the backbone of Egri Bikavér and Szekszárdi Bikavér, and also produces impressive single-variety wines — especially in the cooler northern climate of Sopron and Eger.
What is the origin legend of Egri Bikavér (Bull's Blood)?
A. The wine was originally made to honour a bull-hunting tradition
B. During the 1552 siege of Eger, wine stained the defenders' beards red, leading the Ottoman attackers to believe they had been drinking bull's blood — giving the wine its fearsome name
C. The deep red colour of Kékfrankos resembles bull's blood
D. The wine was named after a famous bull breeder in the Eger region

The most celebrated legend of Egri Bikavér dates to 1552, when Ottoman forces besieged the castle of Eger. The Hungarian defenders, sustained and emboldened by locally made red wine, fought with extraordinary tenacity. Wine staining their beards red, the Ottomans reportedly spread word that the Hungarians were drinking bull's blood — and retreated in fear. Whether or not the story is literally true, it gave the wine its legendary name and character.
What roles do Tokaj's autumn morning fog and warm dry afternoons play in botrytis development?
A. Morning fog lowers temperature to slow ripening; afternoons have no effect
B. The fog provides moisture so Botrytis hyphae can penetrate the grape skin; the warm afternoon evaporates the moisture, concentrating sugars and preventing grey rot
C. Fog and warm afternoons both promote even ripening across the cluster
D. The fog prevents other diseases; the afternoon warmth allows the fog to evaporate

The two-phase microclimate is the engine of Aszú production: morning fog from the Bodrog and Tisza river valleys raises humidity, enabling Botrytis Cinerea hyphae to penetrate Furmint's thin skin; then warm, dry afternoons evaporate the moisture, concentrating sugars, acids and flavours in the berry while preventing the rot from turning grey and destructive. This daily alternation is why Tokaj and only Tokaj consistently produces great botrytis sweet wine.
Which is Villány's most famous grape variety, and what is the name of its official certified brand?
A. Merlot → Villányi Merlot
B. Kékfrankos → Villányi Kékfrankos
C. Cabernet Franc → Villányi Franc
D. Cabernet Sauvignon → Villányi Cabernet

Villány is most celebrated for Cabernet Franc, and the wine carries the official certified designation "Villányi Franc" — the only such certified single-variety brand in Hungary. The combination of Hungary's warmest climate, limestone-rich red clay soils and meticulous estate winemaking allows Villány's Cabernet Franc to achieve remarkable depth and complexity. Wine critic Michael Broadbent famously called Villány the "natural home" of Cabernet Franc.
What effect does Badacsony's basalt volcanic soil have on Olaszrizling?
A. It makes the wines very sweet and low in acidity
B. Strong heat retention plus volcanic minerals absorbed by the vines gives Badacsony Olaszrizling far superior minerality and complexity compared to plains-grown examples
C. It produces wines with very high alcohol
D. The basalt soil causes the vines to ripen earlier

Badacsony's black basalt rock is unique in the Lake Balaton wine landscape. It absorbs solar heat by day and radiates it back at night, creating a warm growing microclimate while the lake cools the air; and the volcanic minerals are taken up by vine roots and expressed in the wine. This is why Badacsony Olaszrizling displays a mineral intensity and structural complexity that is unmatched by the same variety grown on the sandy plains.
What does "6 Puttonyos" traditionally signify in Tokaji Aszú?
A. The wine was aged in barrel for 6 years
B. The wine contains grapes from 6 different vineyards
C. Traditionally, 6 tubs (puttonyos) of Aszú paste were added per 136 litres of base wine — the highest sweetness level
D. The wine has 6% residual sugar

In the traditional Puttonyos system, each tub (puttonyos) of Aszú paste added per 136-litre barrel of base wine represented one level of sweetness. Six Puttonyos was the maximum — producing an intensely concentrated wine with residual sugar above 150 g/L. Since 2013, the Puttonyos number itself is no longer required on the label; instead a minimum residual sugar of 120 g/L qualifies a wine as Tokaji Aszú.
What is the most basic legal requirement for Egri Bikavér?
A. Must be 100% Kékfrankos from the Eger PDO
B. Must come from the Eger PDO, use at least 3 grape varieties, with Kékfrankos as the dominant variety
C. Must be aged in Hungarian oak for a minimum of 3 years
D. Must pass a mandatory blind tasting panel before release

The fundamental legal requirements for Egri Bikavér are: origin from the Eger PDO; a minimum of 3 grape varieties in the blend; and Kékfrankos must represent the highest single percentage. The minimum Kékfrankos share is typically at least 30%, though in practice it is usually over 50%. An additional "Superior" tier exists with stricter criteria, including a mandatory blind tasting panel and longer oak ageing.
